title: Should Investors Buy Iren Instead of Applied Digital? | IREN Stock vs. APLD Stock
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc compares Iren and Applied Digital head to head after upgrading both to buying opportunities a couple of weeks earlier, answering viewers who ask which he prefers. Both are expected to grow revenue sharply for years, with trailing revenue of $707 million for Iren and $854 million for Applied Digital and multi-billion-dollar backlogs, but the key question is what happens at contract renewal if today's supply shortage flips into a glut. On margins, Iren's operating margin is -54% and worsening, while Applied Digital's -24% is improving; on balance sheets, Iren carries $7.84 billion of long-term debt against $7.6 billion of cash and short-term investments, versus $6.5 billion and $3.26 billion for Applied Digital. Valuation favours Iren: forward price-to-sales of 1.3, its lowest in years, against 2.8 for Applied Digital, and his discounted cash flow values Iren at $46 against a $25 price, about 84% undervalued, and Applied Digital at $26.53, also near its 52-week low. If forced to choose, he would rather buy Iren, but calls it a close call and ranks both as buys. The calls are IREN — BUY reiterated and APLD — BUY reiterated, for very-high-risk-tolerance investors only. Note: auto-captions render Iren as 'Iran' throughout.

calls.bear_case: -54% operating margin and worsening; one of the riskiest stocks in the market, extremely volatile, only for very high risk tolerance; renewal / supply-glut risk when contracts expire.
